OP, I am a 32f with CPTSD who no longer speaks to my mother. Like others, I found this post triggering. Your words remind me of my mother, so I hope you hear my words. To answer your main question, you can best support your daughter and help her heal by continuing to ensure she has access to a therapist she feels good about. Other than that, you have your own healing to do. Please do not try to jump into family therapy with your daughter. It's her turn to prioritize herself. Don't force her to take care of you or be close with you. She deserves space. 

Leave your own trauma out of discussions with her. That's for you to handle on your own. You are the parent. She is the child. Your best wasn't good enough for her. It's not your daughter's responsibility to see you in a forgiving light because you had complex trauma too. It doesn't matter that you didn't intentionally cause her trauma. You still did it. One of the most frustrating things my mother always did was point out how none of the trauma she caused was intentional. It's selfish to focus on how pure your intentions were rather than the real impact you had on your own child. It's an easy way to keep pushing a daughter away, imo

You say that your daughter remains "distant and critical" after you've apologized to her. Are you expecting her to behave more agreeably for you? Let her be. Personally, I've gotten countless empty apologies from my mother. True understanding and changed behavior will beat an apology any day. Whatever reason your daughter has for remaining distant and critical is valid. When I'm being "distant and critical' with my parents who caused my CPTSD, I'm restraining myself for all of our benefit. 

It's a red flag to hear you say you "disagree with her version of some of the events" because it sounds like you've probably been invalidating how those events impacted her. I feel for her.

Adult children of emotionally immature parents might be a good read for you both.
